s: In a bisexual flower, if androecium and gynoecium mature at different times, the phenomenon is known as
x: Dichogamy is the maturation of stamens and carpels at different times in a bisexual flower, which promotes cross-pollination. Herkogamy is a physical barrier.

s:
Consider the following statements.

I. Some species of turtles are herbivores.

II. Some species of fish are herbivores.

III. Some species of marine mammals are herbivores.

IV. Some species of snakes are viviparous.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
x: All four statements are true: some turtles, fish and marine mammals (dugong, manatee) are herbivores, and some snakes (e.g. boas, sea snakes) are viviparous.

s: How many covalent bonds are present in a Chloropropane molecule having molecular formula C3H7Cl?
x: C3H7Cl has 2 C–C bonds, 7 C–H bonds and 1 C–Cl bond, totalling 10 covalent bonds.

s: Which one of the following statement is not correct?
o: In steady flow of a liquid, the velocity of liquid particles reaching at a particular point is the same at all points.
Steady flow is also called streamlined flow.
In steady flow, each particle may not follow the same path as taken by a previous particle passing through that point.
Two streamlines cannot intersect with each other.

s: Achaeopteryx is
o: most ancient bird of Jurassic age.
reptile of both Triassic and Jurassic period.
x: Archaeopteryx is the oldest known bird, a feathered reptile-bird link from the Jurassic period.

s:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding common differences between plant and animal cells?

I. Plant cells have cellulose cell wall, while animal cells lack it.

II. Plant cells lack plasma membrane, while animal cells have it.

III. Mature plant cell have a large vacuole, while animal cells have numerous small vacuoles.
x: Plant cells have a cellulose wall and a large central vacuole, while animal cells lack the wall and have small vacuoles. Both cell types have a plasma membrane, so II is wrong.

s: Chromosome number in any species
x: Every species has a fixed, constant chromosome number that does not change with age or weight.

s:
Match the
List I and
List II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists.
List I
List II (Characteristic) (Particle)

A. Zero mass
1. Positron

B. Fractional charge
2. Neutrino

C. Fractional spin
3. Quark

D. Integral spin
4. Photon
Codes A B C D A B C D
x: The neutrino has zero mass, quarks have fractional charge, the positron (a fermion) has half-integral (fractional) spin, and the photon has integral spin (1). This gives 2 3 1 4.

s: Which of these is not a colloid?

Match
List I (Physical quantity) with
List II (Unit) and select the correct answer using codes given below the lists.
List I (Physical quantity)
List II (Unit)

A. Distance
1. Mole

B. Amount of material
2. Coulomb

C. Amount of electrical charge
3. Light year

D. Energy
4. Watt-hour
Codes A B C D
x: Distance is measured in light years, amount of material in moles, charge in coulombs and energy in watt-hours, giving 3 1 2 4.

s: Mammoth is the ancestor of
x: The mammoth was an extinct relative and ancestor of the modern elephant.

s: Which of the following statement is incorrect ?
o: Hydra have only a sexual reproduction.
Most frogs are an oviparous animals.
Internal fertilisation takes place in hens.
x: Hydra reproduces by budding (asexual) and also sexually, so the statement that it has only sexual reproduction is incorrect.

s: Which of the following is a mechanical wave?
x: Sound needs a material medium and is a mechanical wave. Radio waves, X-rays and light are electromagnetic and need no medium.

s:
If the amplitude or oscillation of a simple pendulum is very small, then its time period of oscillation

I. depends on the length of the pendulum, L.

II. depends on the acceleration due to gravity, g.

III. depends upon the mass of the bob of the pendulum, m.

IV. does not depend upon the amplitude of the pendulum, A.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: For small amplitudes T = 2π√(L/g), so it depends on L and g but not on mass or amplitude.

s: Silver gets corroded due to ……… in air.
x: Silver tarnishes by forming black silver sulphide through reaction with hydrogen sulphide in the air.

s: The Leaning Tower of Pisa does not fall because
o: it is tapered at the top.
it covers a large base area.
its centre of gravity remains as the lowest position.
the vertical line through the centre of gravity of the tower falls within its base.
x: A body is stable as long as the vertical line through its centre of gravity falls within its base, which is true for the Leaning Tower of Pisa.

s: Regarding the atom of a chemical element, the magnetic quantum number refers to
x: The magnetic quantum number (m) gives the orientation of an orbital in space. Shape is given by the azimuthal quantum number and size by the principal one.

s:
Consider the following statements X-rays

I. can pass through aluminium.

II. can be deflected by magnetic field.

III. move with a velocity less than the velocity of ultraviolet rays in vacuum.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
x: X-rays are ionising and are not bent by fields, so II is wrong. They travel at the speed of light in vacuum like UV, so III is wrong. They penetrate light metals such as aluminium, so only I is correct.

s: Which of the following elements is not essential for plant growth ?
x: Sodium is not an essential plant nutrient (it is a beneficial element only for some plants), whereas potassium, calcium and magnesium are essential macronutrients.

s: Which one of the following materials is very hard and very ductile?
x: Tungsten is very hard and can be drawn into thin filament wires (bulb filaments), so it is both hard and ductile; carborundum and cast iron are brittle, and nichrome is not very hard.

s:
With reference to the movement of molecules of fluid in plant, consider the following statements.

I. Diffusion is the movement of molecules of a substance from the region of their higher concentration to the region of their lower concentration.

II. Osmosis is a process in which the water molecules move through a semipermeable membrane from the region of their lower concentration to the region of their higher concentration.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct ?

Assertion (A) Whale is a mammal.
Reason (R) Whale has abundant hairs on the body and is a viviparous animal.
Codes
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A whale is a mammal, so A is true. But whales have almost no body hair, so R is false even though they are viviparous.

s: Eight nucleated female gametophyte is found in
x: The angiosperm embryo sac (female gametophyte) typically has 8 nuclei in 7 cells, which is a characteristic of flowering plants.

s: Among living organisms, which one of the following is the most responsible factor for bringing about the origin of a new species?
Which one of the following scales of temperature does not have a negative value?
x: Kelvin is an absolute scale starting at absolute zero (0 K), so it has no negative values; Celsius, Fahrenheit and Reaumur can go below zero.

s:
Assertion (A) All liquids are conductors of electricity.
Reason (R) Under the condition of low pressure and high voltage, liquids can be made conducting.
Codes
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Not all liquids conduct (pure water, oils and many organic liquids are insulators), so A is false. R is a true statement about conduction under low pressure and high voltage.

s: Which of the following has the largest brain in proportion to its body size ?
x: Ants have the largest brain relative to body size in the listed options, taking brain-to-body mass ratio as the measure.

s: Which one of the following elements exist in liquid state at room temperature?
x: Bromine is a liquid at room temperature; hydrogen and oxygen are gases and iodine is a solid. Only bromine and mercury are liquid elements.

s:
Which of the following statement(s) about latent heat for a given substance is/are correct?

I. It is fixed at a given temperature.

II. It depends upon the temperature and volume.

III. It is independent of temperature and volume.

IV. It depends on the temperature but independent of volume.
x: Latent heat of a given substance is fixed for a given temperature and is independent of temperature and volume, so I and III are correct.

s: Which of the following metals is most ductile in nature?
x: Gold is the most ductile metal; it can be drawn into extremely fine wire, more so than silver, copper or aluminium.

s: Which one of the following are useful in the detection of landmines
x: Bees have been trained to detect landmines because of their sharp sense of smell for explosive vapours.

s: Which of the following is an example of chemical change?
o: Dispersion of white light into the light of 7 colours when passed through a prism.
Wet soil lump, when dried, gets fragile.
x: Cooking vegetables causes irreversible changes in their composition (a chemical change). Dispersion, drying of soil and dissolving salt are physical changes.

s: In which one of the following kind of organisms is the phenomenon found where the female kills the male after copulation ?
x: Sexual cannibalism, in which the female kills and eats the male after mating, is typical of spiders such as the black widow.

s: Which one of the following noble gases is not found in the atmosphere?
x: Radon is radioactive and short-lived, and is only present in trace amounts, so it is not counted as a stable atmospheric noble gas as argon, krypton and xenon are.

s: The radius of curvature of the plane mirror is
x: A plane mirror is flat, so its curvature is zero and its radius of curvature is infinity.

s:
Consider the following statements

I. The carat is a unit of purity for gold alloys.

II. 18 carat gold is 24 parts pure gold and 6 parts another metal.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
x: Carat is the measure of gold purity, so I is true. 18 carat gold is 18 parts gold out of 24 (75%), not 24 parts pure gold plus 6 parts other metal, so II is false.

s: Heaviest metal of the following is made of
x: Uranium has by far the highest density among the options, so it is the heaviest metal.

s: Which one of the following is the natural phenomenon based on a simple periscope works?
x: A simple periscope uses two plane mirrors to reflect light, so it works on the reflection of light. Total internal reflection is used in prism periscopes, not in the simple type.

s: Which among the following animals excretes solid urine ?
x: The kangaroo rat, a desert animal, conserves water by excreting highly concentrated, almost solid urine.

s: Which is not a Lewis acid?
x: A Lewis acid accepts an electron pair. AlCl3, BF3 and FeCl3 are electron deficient acceptors, whereas NH3 has a lone pair and acts as a Lewis base.

s:
Consider the following statements about mixture?

I. A substance can be separated into other kinds of matter by any physical process.

II. Dissolved sodium chloride can be separated from water by the physical process of evaporation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
x: Statement I is wrong because a pure substance cannot be separated by physical processes, only a mixture can. Statement II is right because dissolved salt is left behind when water evaporates.

s: Which one of the following is the principal structural elements of a living cell?
x: Carbon is the backbone element of all organic biomolecules (carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acids), so it is the principal structural element of living cells.

s: ‘Archaeopteryx’ is a connecting link between which of the following classes of animal?
x: Archaeopteryx had feathers and wings like birds but also teeth, a long bony tail and clawed fingers like reptiles, so it links Reptilia and Aves.

s: Which gas is known as ‘noble gas’?
x: Helium is a Group 18 inert (noble) gas with a complete outer shell. Hydrogen, oxygen and CO2 are not noble gases.

s: What is the minimum distance (in metres) required to hear an echo?
x: An echo needs a gap of at least 0.1 s between the original sound and its reflection. With sound at about 344 m/s, the sound travels about 34.4 m out and back, so the minimum distance is about 17 m.

s: The number of valence electrons in the O2− ion is
x: O has 6 valence electrons; gaining 2 electrons to form O2− gives a full octet of 8 valence electrons.

s: Crocodiles have a ...... chambered heart.
x: Crocodiles are the only reptiles with a four-chambered heart; other reptiles have three chambers.

s: World first Camel hospital is located in which city?
x: The world's first camel hospital is in Dubai (UAE), the Camel Hospital at Dubai.

s: Which of the following is the electron configuration of a metallic element?
x: The configuration 2, 8, 8, 2 has 2 valence electrons (calcium), which are easily lost, so it is a metal. 2, 8 is neon and 2, 8, 8 is argon (noble gases), while 2, 8, 7 is chlorine, a non-metal.

s:
Which of the following causes the rusting of iron?

I. Oxidation

II. Reduction

III. Chemical reaction with oxygen

IV. Chemical reaction with CO2
x: Rusting is the oxidation of iron through reaction with oxygen (and moisture), so I and III are correct. It is not a reduction, and CO2 is not the cause.

s:
Which one of the following types of medicines is used for treating indigestion?

I. Antibiotic
II. Analgesic

III. Antacid
IV. Antiseptic
Which of the following is not an insects?
x: Spiders are arachnids with 8 legs and two body segments, not insects, which have 6 legs and three body parts. Bed bugs, house flies and mosquitoes are insects.

s: Transfer of heat by convection can take place in
x: Convection needs a material medium whose particles can flow, so it occurs only in fluids (liquids and gases), not in solids or vacuum.

s: The pH value of water is
x: Pure water is neutral, with a pH of 7 at room temperature.

s: The basic difference between an AC generator and a DC generator is that
o: AC generator has an electromagnet while a DC generator has permanent magnet.
AC generator has slip rings while the DC generator has a commutator.
DC generator will generate a higher voltage.
AC generator will generate a higher voltage.
x: An AC generator uses slip rings to deliver alternating current, while a DC generator uses a split-ring commutator to give unidirectional current.

s: Aspirin is obtained from
Among the following which one lays eggs and does not produce young ones directly ?
x: Echidna is a monotreme (egg-laying mammal). Kangaroo, porcupine and whale give birth to young ones.

s: Which one of the following is used in the production of explosives?
x: Glycerol is nitrated to make nitroglycerine, the basis of dynamite and other explosives. Methanol, urea and oxalic acid are not the explosive raw material here.

s:
Match the following.
Quantity SI Unit

A. Frequency
1. Ohm

B. Force
2. Hertz

C. Resistance
3. Newton
Codes A B C
x: Frequency is measured in hertz, force in newton and resistance in ohm, giving A-2, B-3, C-1.

s:
Match
List I with
List II and select the correct answer using codes given below the lists.
List I
List II

A. Photosynthesis
1. Plasma membrane

B. Mineral uptake
2. Chloroplast

C. Respiration
3. Mitochondria

D. Protein synthesis
4. Ribosomes
Codes A B C D
x: Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts, mineral uptake across the plasma membrane, respiration in mitochondria and protein synthesis at ribosomes: A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4.

s: In the context of organic evolution, the loss of limbs in snakes is explained by the phenomenon of

Consider the following sentences.

I. The phenomenon of emission of electrons from metals under the effect of light rays is called photoelectric effect.

II. The electron emitted by the photoelectron effect are called proton.

III. The phenomena like interference diffraction and polarisation were explained successfully on the basis of wave nature of radiation.
Which of the above sentence/sentences is/are correct?
x: Statement I is the correct definition of the photoelectric effect and III is correct because wave nature explains interference, diffraction and polarisation. Statement II is wrong because the emitted particles are photoelectrons, not protons.

s: What is the formula of glucose ?
x: Glucose is a simple sugar (monosaccharide) with the molecular formula C6H12O6; the other formulas given are not glucose.

s: Which of the following is not a vector quantity?
x: Speed has magnitude only, so it is a scalar. Velocity, torque and displacement all have both magnitude and direction, so they are vectors.

s: Which one of these belong to the family in which Panda belong ?
x: The giant panda belongs to the bear family (Ursidae), not the cat, dog or rabbit families.

s: Which one of the following quantities does not have unit?
x: Strain is the ratio of change in length to original length, so it is dimensionless and has no unit. Stress, force and pressure all have units.

s: The foul smell of dead fish is due to the compound
x: Dead fish smell is due to amines such as trimethylamine, formed when bacteria break down the fish, so the answer is amino compounds.

s: Which one of the following elements is present in the green pigment of leaves?
x: Chlorophyll, the green pigment of leaves, has magnesium at the centre of its porphyrin ring.

s: The sound will have the highest velocity in
x: Sound travels fastest in solids such as steel because they are the most elastic and rigid, and it cannot travel through a vacuum at all.

s:
Match
List I with
List II and select the correct answer using codes given below the lists.
List I
List II

A. Acceleration
1. Joule

B. Force
2. Newton second

C. Work done
3. Newton

D. Impulse
4. Metre per second2
Codes A B C D A B C D
x: Acceleration is measured in metre per second squared, force in newton, work in joule and impulse in newton second. This gives the code 4 3 1 2.

s: A hot body cools from 90°C to 75°C in 25 second. The same body in further cooling from 75°C to 60°C will take how much time?
x: By Newton's law of cooling, the rate of cooling falls as the body gets closer to the surroundings' temperature. The same 15°C drop therefore takes more than 25 s.

s: Solar energy is converted into ATP in

After using for some time, big transformers get heated up. This is due to the fact that

I. current produces heat in the transformers.

II. hysteresis loss occurs in the transformers.

III. liquid used for cooling gets heated.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Transformer heating comes from I²R (copper) losses from the current and from hysteresis (core) losses. Coolant liquid heating is an effect, not a cause, so statement III is wrong.

s:
Consider the following four particles

I. Alpha particle
II. Proton

III. Electron
IV. Neutron
Which of the following is the correct sequence in which their rest masses increase?
x: The electron is lightest, then the proton, then the neutron (slightly heavier than the proton), and the alpha particle (2 protons + 2 neutrons) is heaviest: III-II-IV-I.

s:
Match
List I with
List II and select the correct answer using codes given below the lists.
List I
List II (Units) (Parametric quantities)

A. Watt
1. Heat

B. Knot
2. Navigation

C. Nautical mile
3. Speed of a ship

D. Calorie
4. Power
Codes A B C D A B C D
x: Watt is the unit of power, knot is the speed of a ship, nautical mile is used in navigation and calorie is a unit of heat, giving 4 3 2 1.

s: The cellular and molecular control of programmed cell death is known as
x: Apoptosis is genetically controlled programmed cell death. Necrosis is uncontrolled death caused by injury.

s: World’s first camel hospital is located in which city?
x: The world's first camel hospital is in Dubai, UAE.

s: The most reactive among the halogen is
x: Reactivity of halogens decreases down the group, so fluorine, the most electronegative element, is the most reactive.

s: The speed of sound is faster in
x: Sound travels fastest in solids, which are the most elastic and dense in particle packing, slower in liquids and gases, and not at all in a vacuum.

s: Which one of the following pairs constitutes particle-antiparticle pair?
x: The positron is the antiparticle of the electron, with the same mass and opposite charge. The other pairs are not particle-antiparticle pairs.

s: Which of the following organisms has White blood ?
x: The cockroach has colourless (whitish) haemolymph because it lacks haemoglobin, so its blood does not look red.

s: Which is not a primary colour?
x: The primary colours of light are red, green and blue, and of pigments are red, yellow and blue. Black is not a primary colour.

s: Which one of the following statement is not correct?
o: The SI unit of charge is ampere- second.
Debye is the unit of dipole moment.
Resistivity of a wire of length I and area of cross-section A depends upon both I and A.
The kinetic energy of an electron of mass m kilogram and charge e coulomb, when accelerated through a potential difference of V volt is eV joule.
x: Resistivity (ρ = RA/l) is a property of the material, not of the wire's length or cross-section area, so statement 3 is incorrect. The other statements are standard facts.

s: The reason of large scale diversity among the organisms is
A bacteriophage is a
x: A bacteriophage is a virus that infects bacteria (phage = 'eater' of bacteria). The option describing a bacterium-infecting virus is the right one; the others wrongly call it a bacterium.

s: The minimum distance of clear vision for a normal healthy eye of human being is supposed to be
x: The least distance of distinct vision for a normal human eye is about 25 cm, so 25 cm is correct.

s: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to stigma of another flower of the same plant is called ?
x: Geitonogamy is pollen transfer from the anther to the stigma of a different flower on the same plant. Autogamy occurs within the same flower and xenogamy between flowers of different plants.

s: Which one of the following is not the unit of heat?
x: Calorie, erg and joule are units of heat/energy, whereas centigrade is a temperature scale, not a unit of heat.

s: Which of the following cell organelles play the most significant role in protein synthesis?
x: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis, and the rough endoplasmic reticulum, which carries ribosomes, helps synthesise and process proteins. So ER and ribosome is correct.

s:
Consider the following statements

I. Homologous organs are common origin with different functions.

II. Analogous organs are different origin but perform similar function in different organisms.

III. Vestigial organs are non-functional and rudimentary organs in an organism which are fully developed and functional in phylogenetically related organisms.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three statements are correct definitions: homologous organs share origin but may differ in function, analogous organs differ in origin but are similar in function, and vestigial organs are reduced, non-functional remnants.

s: With the rise of temperature, the viscosity of liquid
o: may increase or decrease depending on nature of liquid
x: As temperature rises, molecules of a liquid gain kinetic energy and intermolecular cohesive forces weaken, so viscosity decreases. (In gases viscosity increases.)

s: Which one of the following is a membrane that protects the developing embryo from desiccation?
x: The amnion encloses the embryo in amniotic fluid, protecting it from desiccation and shock. Allantois handles excretion/respiration, chorion is the outer membrane, and the yolk sac holds nutrients.

s: Which of the following is poisonous for dogs?
x: Chocolate contains theobromine, which dogs metabolise much more slowly than humans, making it toxic to them.

s: The broad, green part of the leaf is called
x: The lamina (leaf blade) is the broad, flat, green part of the leaf where photosynthesis mainly occurs; the midrib is the central vein and the petiole is the stalk.

s: The broad , green part of the leaf is called
x: The lamina (leaf blade) is the broad, flat, green part of the leaf; the petiole is the stalk and the midrib and veins are the supporting and conducting structures.

s: Angstrom is a/an:
x: The angstrom is a unit of length equal to 10^-10 metres.

s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
I. Coelenterates, ctenophores and echinoderms have radical symmetry kind of body plan.
II. Sponges are mostly asymmetrical.
o: Both I and II are correct
Both I and II are not correct
x: Coelenterates, ctenophores and echinoderms (adults show pentamerous radial symmetry) are radially symmetrical, and sponges are mostly asymmetrical, so both statements are correct.

s: What does the following sign indicate? (a cross symbol)
x: A cross symbol is the standard sign for first aid, not for a hospital, crossroad or no parking.

s: Ants are social insects because
x: Ants are social insects because they live in organised colonies with division of labour (queen, workers, soldiers).

s: Pearls are the products from:
x: Pearls are formed inside molluscs such as oysters, which secrete layers of nacre around an irritant.

s: 'Circumvallation' is a phenomenon concerned with which of the following events?
x: Circumvallation is a method of ingestion (food capture) in Amoeba, where pseudopodia surround the prey.

s: Which of the following creatures are stone-deaf?
x: Snakes lack external ears and eardrums, so they cannot hear airborne sound; they instead sense vibrations through the ground.

s: At what age does bamboo flower?
What percentage of gold is there in 14 carat gold?
x: Pure gold is 24 carat, so 14 carat gold has 14/24 ≈ 58.3% gold. This is consistent with 22 carat = 91.6% and 18 carat = 75%.

s: Magnification produced by a rear view mirror fitted in vehicles —
x: A rear-view mirror is a convex mirror, whose magnification is always less than one, giving a wide field of view with diminished images.

s: Maximum Photosynthesis occurs in:
x: The maximum rate of photosynthesis is generally recorded in red light of the visible spectrum.

s: The velocity of sound is highest
o: In dry air at 0 degrees centigrade
In dry air at 30 degrees centigrade
In moist air at 0 degrees centigrade
In moist air at 30 degrees centigrade
x: Sound speed increases with temperature and also with moisture, since moist air is less dense than dry air. So moist air at 30 °C has the highest speed.

s: Which of the following are generally formed in combustion of saturated hydrocarbons?
x: Combustion of saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) generally gives carbon dioxide, water and heat (and light); carbon/soot forms only in incomplete combustion, so the standard NCERT answer is option 3 (I could not open the official APPSC key to confirm what it says).

src: APPSC 2021 Medical Officer (Ayurveda) In Ayush Department
s:
Given below are the two statements marked as
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R). Analyze the statements and choose one of the given options.
Assertion (A): We see a blue sky most of the time.
Reason (R): Sunlight reaches Earth's atmosphere and is always concentrated. Blue light is concentrated more than the other colors as it travels in long, lazy waves.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
x: The blue sky is a real observation, so A is true. R is false: it is Rayleigh scattering of the short-wavelength blue light by air molecules that makes the sky blue, not blue light being 'concentrated' or travelling in long lazy waves.

s: The substance coated on plastic tape-recorder tapes is
x: Magnetic recording tape is a plastic tape coated with iron oxide (ferric oxide) particles.

s: The astronaut in the ship sees the sky as:
x: In the absence of an atmosphere to scatter sunlight, an astronaut in space sees a black sky even during daytime.

s: If the cover of a book looks red when seen through a piece of red glass, then the cover will look like
x: Red glass transmits only red light. A red cover reflects red light and looks red; a white cover reflects all colours but only red passes through, so it also looks red. Hence the cover may be red or white.

s: The flying of birds is a proof of Newton's
x: Birds push air downward and backward with their wings (action) and the air pushes them upward and forward (reaction). This is Newton's third law.

s: We obtain chilgoza from the seed of species –
x: Pinus gerardiana is the biological name of chilgoza pine. Chilgoza is rich in carbohydrate and protein and it is obtained from pine seeds.

s: In an atom, the order of filling up of the orbitals is governed by –
x: The Aufbau principle is used to determine the electron configuration of an atom, molecule or ion. The principle postulates a hypothetical process in which an atom is 'built up' by progressively adding electrons. As they are added, they assume their most stable condition (electron orbitals) with respect to the nucleus and those electrons already there. According to the principle, electrons fill orbitals starting at the lowest available (possible) energy levels before filling higher levels (e.g. 1s before 2s).

s: The SI unit of electrical resistivity of conductor is –
x: The SI unit of electrical resistivity is the ohm-metre, so Ohm is the only option related to it.

s: What is the unit of atmospheric pressure?
x: Bar is metric (but not SI) unit of pressure. It is equal to 105 newton/metre2. Pascal is SI unit of pressure. 1 bar = 105 Pascal.

s: Which one of the following statements is not true about cosmic rays?
o: They are made of highly energetic charged particles
x: Cosmic rays are streams of highly energetic charged particles (mainly protons) and not electromagnetic waves, so the statement that they are electromagnetic waves is the untrue one.

s: Which one of the following instrument is used for locating submerged objects in an ocean ?
x: SONAR [Sound Navigation and Ranging] is used for locating submerged objects in an ocean. It is based on a very simple principle i.e. pulse of ultrasonic waves is sent into the water, it strikes the target and bounced back towards the source. It helps to detect or locate submerged submarines and icebergs.

s: What is the unit of measure of magnetic field?
x: A magnetic field (sometimes called B-field) is a physical field that describes the magnetic influence on moving electric charges, electric currents, and magnetic materials. In electromagnetics, the term magnetic field is used for two distinct but closely related vector fields denoted by the symbols B and H. In the International System of Units (SI), the unit of B, magnetic flux density (also called magnetic B-field), is the tesla (Symbol : T; in SI base units : kilogram per second squared per ampere), which is equivalent to newton per ampere-meter. The unit of H, magnetic field strength, is ampere per meter (A/m). B and H differ in how they take the medium and/or magnetization into account.

s: Bats can fly during dark nights and also prey. This is because :
o: The pupil of their eyes is large
Their night vision is very good
They produce ultrasonic waves and are guided by
x: Bats are a fascinating group of animals. They are one of the few mammals that can use ultrasonic sound to navigate. As they fly, make an ultrasonic (shouting) sound. The returning echoes give the bats information about anything that is ahead of them, including the speed and size of an insect and which way it is going. This system of finding prey is called echolocationlocating things by their echoes.

s: By which one of the following an old written material which cannot be read easily, can be read?
x: Infrared radiation is used in heat therapy and imaging; it is the radiation that can bring out faded or hard-to-read writing, unlike gamma rays, X-rays or radio waves, which are not used for this.

s: Which of the following is attracted to the North pole of a permanent magnet?
o: North pole of another permanent magnet
A piece of iron that is not a permanent magnet
x: Unmagnetised iron is attracted by either pole of a magnet, so a non-magnet iron piece is attracted to the north pole, whereas like poles repel and charged rods are not affected by magnets.

s: For two liquids A and B to form an ideal solution :
o: Entropy of mixing must be zero
Free energy of mixing should be zero
Enthalpy of mixing should be zero
x: An ideal solution is a homogeneous mixture where the interactions between solute and solvent molecules are identical to those between the pure components. This means that the intermolecular forces between solute and solvent molecules are roughtly the same as the intermolecular forces between solute-solute and solvent-solvent molecules. For an ideal solution, the enthalpy of mixing (ΔHmix) is zero. The enthalpy of mixing (ΔHmix) is the change in enthalpy that occurs when a substance is mixed with another substance or when a solution is formed. In an ideal solution, since the interactions between molecules are similar, there is no net change in energy when the components are mixed. Therefore, the enthalpy of mixing is zero. This means that when the components of an ideal solution are mixed, there is no heat absorbed or released. In essence, the molecules mix without any energy change. The ideal solution follows Raoult's Law, which states that the partial vapour pressure of each component in the solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction.

s: The reverse effect of X-ray emission is

s: Which of the following underground produced vegetables is a modified root ?
x: The sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) is a dicotyledonous plant that belongs to the family Convolvulaceae. Sweet potato is a modified root cultivated by vegetative propagation.

s: The amount of solute present per unit volume or per unit mass of the solution/solvent is known as ____ in Chemistry.
x: The amount of solute present per unit volume or per unit mass of the solution/solvent is called 'Concentration of Solution'. The concentration of a solution is the measure of how much solute is present in a fixed amount (mass or volume) of the solution or the amount of solute dissolved in a given mass or volume of solvent.

s: Viagra is the brand name of the drug that improves sexual energy in men. What is its chemical name?
x: Sildenafil citrate Viagra's active pharmaceutical ingredient is sildenafil citrate, a PDE5 inhibitor that increases blood flow, and it is marketed worldwide under this and related brand names.

s: Lead Pencil contains –
x: The pencil 'lead' is actually graphite, a form of carbon, not the metal lead or its compounds.

s: An example of physical change –
x: Physical changes usually affect the form of a chemical substance, but not its chemical composition. This fact contrasts with the concept of chemical change in which the chemical composition of the substance changes or one or more substances combines or break up to form new substances. In general, a physical change is using physical means. For example, sugar dissolved in water can be recovered by allowing the water to evaporate.

s: To which group of plants does the Banyan Tree belong?
x: The banyan is a flowering plant that bears seeds enclosed in fruits (figs), so it is an angiosperm, not a gymnosperm, pteridophyte or alga.

s: In plants, active cell division occurs in the following parts
x: In plants, active cell division primarily occurs in the meristematic tissues found in roots and shoot tips. Root apical meristems specifically drive elongation and branching of the root system.

s: Which one of the following is a secretion from the body of an insect ?
x: Lac is the scarlet resinous secretion of a number of species of lac insects, of which the most commonly cultivated species is Kerria lacca. Cultivation begins when a farmer gets a stick (brood lac) that contains eggs ready to hatch and ties it to the tree to be infested.Thousands of lac insects colonize the branches of the host trees and secrete the resinous pigment. It is used in the manufacture of varnishes, sealing wax, shellac etc.
